places.name: Tivoli Gardens
places.description: The 6-year-old rides carousels, the pirate ship and gentle kids' rides in the family zone, while the 1-year-old naps in the pram or crawls on the lakeside lawns away from the ride noise. Evening lights and free daytime entertainment suit both ages without needing every ride.
places.baby_notes: Quiet lakeside garden paths let a pram nap happen away from ride noise and crowds.
places.tips: Arrive at opening to beat queues for the children's rides.

places.name: The Little Mermaid
places.description: A quick free stop where the 6-year-old can spot the bronze mermaid on her harbour rock and hear the Hans Christian Andersen story, while the 1-year-old toddles along the flat promenade railing. Best treated as a photo stop rather than a destination in itself.
places.baby_notes: Promenade is flat and pram-friendly; keep baby off the wet rocks right by the statue.
places.tips: Go early morning to see the statue without tour-bus crowds.

places.name: Nyhavn
places.description: The 6-year-old counts the brightly coloured 17th-century townhouses and watches the canal boats and street performers, while the 1-year-old can toddle short stretches of the flat quayside between benches. Canal-front lunch spots make it an easy midday stop with a pram.
places.baby_notes: Quayside is flat but cobbled — expect a bumpy pram ride; benches every few metres for a stop.
places.tips: Restaurants on the sunny side of the canal fill up fast at lunchtime — book or arrive before noon.

places.name: Rosenborg Castle
places.description: The 6-year-old can hunt for the Crown Jewels and royal treasures in the Treasury vault and imagine kings and queens in the turreted rooms. The 1-year-old is better left in a carrier rather than the pram, since the castle's original staircases are narrow and steep.
places.baby_notes: Narrow original staircases mean no pram inside — carry baby in a front or back carrier.
places.tips: Book a timed entry slot online in advance — summer slots sell out.

places.name: Christiansborg Palace – The Royal Reception Rooms
places.description: The 6-year-old can admire the giant tapestries telling 1,000 years of Danish history and the gilded Throne Room. The 1-year-old is best carried rather than pushed, as the reception rooms are reached by grand staircases with no lift for prams.
places.baby_notes: Grand staircases with no pram access — plan to carry baby through the reception rooms.
places.tips: Combine with the free Christiansborg tower view a few doors along if energy allows.

places.name: The Round Tower (Rundetaarn)
places.description: The 6-year-old climbs the famous spiral ramp — no steps — to reach a rooftop view over the city's coloured rooftops. The 1-year-old can go up in the pram along the same ramp, though there is no floor space to crawl at the top.
places.baby_notes: The spiral ramp (built for horse carriages) takes a pram all the way up, but there's no safe crawling space at the viewing platform.
places.tips: Go late afternoon for softer light over the rooftops and thinner queues.

places.name: Den Blå Planet (National Aquarium Denmark)
places.description: The 6-year-old can walk through the shark and ocean tunnel and touch rays in the touch pool. The 1-year-old can crawl safely on the flat, wide walkways or nap in the pram in the dim, quiet tunnel sections.
places.baby_notes: Flat, buggy-friendly floors throughout; the dim ocean tunnel is a good spot for a pram nap.
places.tips: Book online for a timed slot — the shark tank feeding times draw the biggest crowds.

places.name: Copenhagen Zoo
places.description: The 6-year-old can ride a pony and play in the Kaninbyen (Rabbit City) climbing labyrinth, then watch elephants and polar bears. The 1-year-old can crawl on the grass in the Children's Zoo petting area away from paths and prams.
places.baby_notes: Grass areas in the Children's Zoo are safe for crawling, away from main path traffic.
places.tips: Feeding times for the elephants and sea lions are posted at the entrance — plan the route around them.

places.name: Experimentarium
places.description: The 6-year-old gets hands-on with bubble, water and gravity experiments built for children. The 1-year-old has a dedicated small-children's play area with soft flooring to crawl and explore safely away from the bigger exhibits.
places.baby_notes: A soft-floored small-children's zone is set apart from the busier hands-on exhibits.
places.tips: Book online in advance for a 10% discount and a guaranteed entry slot.

places.name: National Museum of Denmark – Children's Museum
places.description: The 6-year-old can dress up, sail a Viking ship replica and cook in a mock medieval kitchen, all designed to be touched and played with. The 1-year-old can crawl on the mats in the ground-floor Children's Museum wing, which is flat and pram-accessible.
places.baby_notes: Ground-floor Children's Museum has soft play mats safe for crawling, and is fully pram-accessible.
places.tips: Head straight for the Children's Museum wing first — it's the main draw for this age group.

places.name: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark
places.description: The 6-year-old hunts for animals hidden in old master paintings and can join the free weekend Atelier des Enfants drawing sessions. The 1-year-old can crawl and cruise in the carpeted family relaxation corner, which has books and floor games set out on weekdays.
places.baby_notes: Carpeted family relaxation corner (weekdays) has floor space and books for a crawling baby.
places.tips: Permanent collection is free; only special exhibitions charge admission.

places.name: Designmuseum Danmark
places.description: The 6-year-old follows a free activity booklet guided by "Kay the monkey", spotting shapes and patterns in Danish furniture and textiles and drawing their own designs. The 1-year-old can be wheeled or toddle through the dedicated children's play areas set up around the galleries.
places.baby_notes: Dedicated children's play stations dotted through the galleries give a toddler room to move.
places.tips: Pick up the free children's game booklet at the ticket office before starting the visit.

places.name: Danish Architecture Center (DAC), BLOX
places.description: The 6-year-old can ride the 40-metre indoor DAC Slide and follow a children's trail through the architecture exhibitions. The 1-year-old stays dry inside BLOX's wide, stroller-friendly halls even if rain rules out the adjoining outdoor playground.
places.tips: The Carve-designed playground outside is a bonus if the rain eases, but the ticket covers the indoor exhibitions and DAC Slide regardless.

places.name: Natural History Museum of Denmark
places.description: The 6-year-old can touch a real meteorite and piece together a skeleton in the Mineral Hall. The 1-year-old needs to be carried through, since personal strollers stay parked in the courtyard rather than coming into the exhibition.
places.tips: Personal prams must be left in the courtyard before entering the exhibition halls, so plan to carry or babywear.

places.name: The Workers Museum (Arbejdermuseet)
places.description: The 6-year-old takes a paid "job" at the 1930s brewery or bicycle-messenger post in the Children's Workers' Museum and can join the weekend treasure hunt. The 1-year-old can nap in the pram through the atmospheric tenement rooms, which the museum says are largely wheelchair (and so pram) accessible.
places.tips: The Children's Workers' Museum section is aimed at ages 3-12 and includes a weekend treasure hunt around the exhibitions.

places.name: Museum of Copenhagen (Københavns Museum)
places.description: The 6-year-old can follow the free, kid-made children's guide on a self-led trail through the city's Viking and medieval history. The 1-year-old's own pram gets swapped for a museum-issued one before the exhibition rooms, so plan to carry them for short stretches.
places.tips: Free admission every Wednesday; own prams must be left at the cloakroom and swapped for a museum stroller before the exhibition rooms.

places.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.description: The 6-year-old can hunt for mummies and Roman busts before cooling off among the palms of the domed Winter Garden. The 1-year-old's own pram is stored at the entrance in exchange for a loaner, so budget a moment for the swap on arrival.
places.tips: Private strollers aren't allowed for security reasons, but the museum lends one for the visit while yours is stored.

places.name: Thorvaldsens Museum
places.description: The 6-year-old wanders among Thorvaldsen's marble gods and heroes in brightly coloured, easy-to-love rooms right on Slotsholmen. The 1-year-old needs to be carried between the three floors, since there's no lift and the doorways only fit the museum's own umbrella-style strollers.
places.tips: Free entry every Wednesday; there's no lift between floors, and doorways are narrow, so an own pram may not fit.

places.name: ENIGMA – Museum of Communication
places.description: The 6-year-old can play postman, tap out a telegram on a typewriter, and crawl through the communication-themed Teleportalen play zone (ages 3-10). The 1-year-old can be wheeled straight in from Trianglen Metro station and watch the play area from a pram or lap under supervision.
places.tips: The Teleportalen play zone is aimed at ages 3-10, so a 1-year-old will mostly watch from the edges rather than play unsupervised.

places.name: Kunsthal Charlottenborg
places.description: The 6-year-old gets an easy, low-key introduction to contemporary art wandering the big open gallery floors just off Nyhavn. The 1-year-old can be wheeled or carried throughout in their own pram, and there's a proper changing table plus space to breastfeed or bottle-feed.
places.baby_notes: Own pram is welcome throughout the galleries and a changing table is in the accessible restroom.
places.tips: Free admission Wednesday evenings 17:00-20:00; children 0-15 are always free.

places.name: Frederiksberg Svømmehal & Spa
places.description: Indoor pool complex with a 12m children's pool at chest-height depth for the 6-year-old and a dedicated timed baby basin where the 1-year-old can splash while held. Ground-floor changing rooms make arriving with a pram straightforward.
places.baby_notes: Baby basin (timed 25-minute slots) lets the 1-year-old paddle in warm shallow water held by an adult.
places.tips: Book the baby basin slot ahead if visiting during peak summer holiday hours.

places.name: Vandkulturhuset, DGI-byen
places.description: Five indoor pool zones a short walk from Central Station, including a warm shallow dipping pool the 6-year-old can wade through and gentle enough water for the 1-year-old to be held in. Fully indoor and reachable on foot without a car.
places.baby_notes: Warm shallow pool zone suits a supervised toddler in arm-floats; no dedicated baby-only basin confirmed.
places.tips: Arrive right at opening to beat queues during the summer holiday week.

places.name: DGI-byen Bowling
places.description: Sixteen lanes with bumpers and light balls let the 6-year-old bowl properly, while the 1-year-old can toddle around the flat, carpeted lane area under close supervision. Same building as the pool, easy to combine on a rainy day.
places.tips: Book a lane ahead — summer holiday slots fill fast.

places.name: Blocs & Walls
places.description: The Nordics' largest bouldering gym has a dedicated kids' climbing wall (minimum age 4) that suits the 6-year-old, plus a café where an adult can sit with the 1-year-old on a mat nearby. It's a bus ride from the centre, not metro-served.
places.tips: Take the 9A bus from Østerport or Nørreport; there's no metro stop at Refshaleøen.

places.name: Airtrix Trampolinpark & Klatrepark Nordhavn
places.description: Indoor trampoline and climbing park where the 6-year-old can jump and climb; the 1-year-old is too young for the trampolines but can sit safely in the café/seating area while the rest of the family takes turns.
places.tips: Book online ahead; weekend sessions fill up.

places.name: JumpYard Field's
places.description: Indoor trampoline park inside Field's shopping centre, fully weatherproof and metro-side. The 6-year-old can jump (minimum age 3) while the 1-year-old naps in the pram in the adjoining food court.
places.tips: Book online ahead — walk-in costs more per person than a pre-booked slot.

places.name: Dinos Legeland Ørestad
places.description: Purpose-built indoor soft-play centre with ball pits, slides and toys sorted by age, directly opposite Vestamager metro. The 6-year-old has a full-size play structure and the 1-year-old (free under age 1) has a separate crawling/toddler zone.
places.baby_notes: Dedicated toddler soft-play zone separate from the bigger kids' structure lets the 1-year-old crawl and cruise safely.
places.tips: No time limit per visit, so it works well as a flexible rainy-afternoon filler.

places.name: Bellahøj Svømmestadion
places.description: Municipal pool complex with an indoor shallow play pool (5x12m, 0.8m deep) where the 6-year-old can wade and play, shallow enough for an adult to hold the 1-year-old in the water. Quieter and less central than the DGI-byen pools.
places.baby_notes: Shallow 0.8m indoor play pool is safe for an adult to hold the 1-year-old in the water.

places.name: Cinemateket – Børnebiffen
places.description: Free short-film screenings curated for ages 3-7 at the Danish Film Institute's cinema, a good fit for the 6-year-old on a rainy morning. The 1-year-old is below the target age, but the short, dark, indoor screenings work fine for a pram nap.
places.tips: Check the current programme online — Børnebiffen only runs on select days.

places.name: The King's Garden (Kongens Have)
places.description: Denmark's oldest royal garden, right by Rosenborg Castle, with broad lawns and a vintage wooden playground. The 6-year-old can climb the play equipment and spot the marionette theatre; the 1-year-old can practise walking on flat gravel paths or crawl on open lawn under the trees.
places.baby_notes: Broad lawns near the playground give a soft, flat spot for a crawling baby; a café on site sells snacks.
places.tips: Arrive before midday in summer to get a bench near the playground before it fills up.

places.name: Frederiksberg Gardens (Frederiksberg Have)
places.description: A romantic English-style landscape garden with canals, bridges and a Chinese pavilion, next to Copenhagen Zoo. The 6-year-old can hunt for the Chinese Pavilion and watch the canal boats; the 1-year-old can crawl on the open lawns or nap in the pram under shady avenues.
places.baby_notes: Grassy picnic lawns near the canal give a safe, flat spot to sit or crawl away from the water's edge.
places.tips: Combine with the adjoining Søndermarken if the family wants a longer flat walk.

places.name: Amager Beach Park (Amager Strandpark)
places.description: A 4.6km stretch of sandy beach and man-made lagoon with a shallow toddler-friendly side. The 6-year-old can paddle and dig in the sand; the 1-year-old, just starting to walk, can practise steps barefoot on the soft sand near the shallow lagoon edge.
places.baby_notes: Soft sand well back from the lagoon is safe for crawling and early walking; bring shade for the pram.
places.tips: Metro M2 stops directly at Amager Strand station a short walk from the sand.

places.name: Islands Brygge Harbour Bath (Havnebadet)
places.description: A lifeguard-supervised open-air harbour bath with five pools, two of them shallow and built for children. The 6-year-old can swim and use the diving steps in the kids' pools; the 1-year-old can sit and splash in the 30cm-deep pool or crawl on the surrounding lawn.
places.baby_notes: Lawn strip beside the pools is a safe, flat spot to sit a baby away from open water; lifeguards on duty June-August.
places.tips: Open May 1 to Sep 30; lifeguards present only June 1 - Aug 31, 10:00-18:00.

places.name: Superkilen
places.description: A striking, colourful urban park split into a red urban square, a black market plaza and a green lawn area, with playground pieces gathered from around the world. The 6-year-old can climb the Japanese octopus slide and Iraqi swings; the 1-year-old can crawl on the flat Green Park lawn.
places.baby_notes: The Green Park zone is open lawn, flat and safe for a crawling or early-walking baby.
places.tips: The octopus slide and swings get busy after school hours; go earlier in the day.

places.name: Assistens Cemetery (Assistens Kirkegård)
places.description: A leafy park-cemetery where locals picnic and sunbathe among the graves of Hans Christian Andersen and Søren Kierkegaard. The 6-year-old can hunt for famous headstones along the meandering paths; the 1-year-old can crawl on the meadow grass away from the graves.
places.baby_notes: Open meadow areas away from headstones offer flat grass safe for crawling.
places.tips: Open 7:00-22:00 in summer; keep to the paths as it remains an active cemetery.

places.name: Tower Playground, Fælledparken
places.description: A themed playground in Copenhagen's second-largest park, built as five scaled-down versions of the city's famous towers. The 6-year-old can climb the Round Tower and Town Hall Tower replicas and play electronic tag; the 1-year-old can crawl on the grass bordering the sandbox.
places.baby_notes: Grass around the sandbox area is flat and safe for a baby to sit or crawl while an older sibling climbs.
places.tips: The manned building (10:00-15:30) lends sandbox toys and balls from April to October.

places.name: Botanical Garden (Botanisk Have)
places.description: The University of Copenhagen's botanical garden, with historic 1874 glasshouses including a Palm House, useful shelter on a showery day. The 6-year-old can explore the tropical Palm House and spot exotic plants; the 1-year-old can crawl on the outdoor lawns or nap in the pram under the glasshouse roof if it rains.
places.baby_notes: Lawns near the glasshouses are flat and open for crawling; the Palm House gives genuine cover from rain.
places.tips: Glasshouses close earlier than the outdoor garden, so visit them first if short on time.

places.name: Valby Park (Valbyparken)
places.description: Copenhagen's largest park, with themed gardens, a nature playground and wide picnic lawns. The 6-year-old can explore the nature playground and rose garden; the 1-year-old can crawl on the open picnic lawns or practise walking on the flat paths between the theme gardens.
places.baby_notes: Wide picnic lawns throughout the park give plenty of flat, open grass for a crawling baby.
places.tips: It's a big park with few signs, so plan the route in advance to reach the nature playground directly.

places.name: Kastellet (The Citadel)
places.description: A star-shaped 17th-century fortress with grassy ramparts, a windmill and a moat, doubling as a peaceful public park. The 6-year-old can run along the ramparts and spot the windmill; the 1-year-old can crawl on the grassy embankments away from the moat edge.
places.baby_notes: Grassy ramparts away from the moat edge are flat enough for crawling, though keep a close eye near the water.
places.tips: Open daily 06:00-22:00; the Changing of the Guard happens around noon.

places.name: Church of Our Saviour (Vor Frelsers Kirke)
places.description: 6-year-old climbs famous spiral spire (400 steps, no lift) with one adult for harbour views; other adult stays with 1-year-old on safe stone floor of free, pram-accessible ground-floor church.
places.baby_notes: Ground-floor church safe stone floor for baby to sit; spiral stairs unusable with baby or pram.
places.tips: Book tower slot ahead via Billetto to skip queue; bells ring loud 18:00 daily.

places.name: Amalienborg Palace Square – Changing of the Guard
places.description: 6-year-old watches marching band and guards parade square at noon; 1-year-old toddles flat cobbles from pram, kept back from guards.
places.baby_notes: Flat paved square safe underfoot; keep 2m back from guards, expect crowds near noon.
places.tips: Arrive 11:30 — parade departs barracks 11:27, reaches square noon.

places.name: Ofelia Plads
places.description: 6-year-old watches harbour traffic and Opera House from tiered wooden decking; 1-year-old has flat boards to toddle across away from water's edge.
places.baby_notes: Flat decking safe for walking practice well away from un-railed water's edge; pavilion café/toilets nearby give brief shelter.
places.tips: Watch 1-year-old closely near uneven steps by water.

places.name: GoBoat Copenhagen
places.description: 6-year-old helps steer electric picnic boat around canals; 1-year-old rides on lap with properly fitted life vest — pram stays onshore for this one.
places.baby_notes: Check GoBoat life-vest sizing for 1-year-old before booking; open-air, no shelter, pram cannot come aboard.
places.tips: Book online ahead; driver must be 18+.

places.name: Netto-Bådene Canal and Harbour Tour
places.description: 6-year-old gets full hour narrated sightseeing past canals and harbour; 1-year-old held rather than left in pram during moving boat ride.
places.baby_notes: Covered cabin section for shelter; fold pram before boarding, hold 1-year-old rather than leave seated alone.
places.tips: Online ticket slightly cheaper than kiosk; departures every 20-30 min in August.

places.name: Copenhagen Harbour Bus (Havnebus 991/992)
places.description: Cheap no-fuss boat ride 6-year-old enjoys for harbour views; pram kept fully assembled in confirmed stroller space, 1-year-old seated for covered crossing.
places.baby_notes: Each boat carries up to 4 strollers, covered cabin — good nap-timed crossing, keep baby seated while underway.
places.tips: Covered by standard Rejsekort/DOT ticket — no extra fare over normal bus.

places.name: Freetown Christiania
places.description: 6-year-old loves colourful hand-built houses and street art on self-guided walk; 1-year-old better carried than pushed since paths cobbled and unpaved in places.
places.baby_notes: Uneven unpaved paths in places — all-terrain pram or carrier works better than standard stroller.
places.tips: No photography on Pusher Street.

places.name: Christianshavns Vold (Rampart of Christianshavn)
places.description: 6-year-old runs freely along open grass rampart with water views; 1-year-old has flat safe ground to crawl or practise walking away from traffic.
places.baby_notes: Grassy rampart paths flat and safe for baby to crawl or take first steps under supervision.
places.tips: Quiet stop for nap-timed pram walk along water, open 24/7.

places.name: Islands Brygge Havnepark
places.description: 6-year-old plays on equipment and open lawns; 1-year-old crawls or practises walking safely on grass, with Cultural Centre nearby for shelter if it rains.
places.baby_notes: Flat lawns and paved paths safe for crawling and first steps; adjacent Cultural Centre building offers indoor shelter.
places.tips: Grass and playground area — distinct from Harbour Bath swimming pools next door.

places.name: Amager Fælled
places.description: 6-year-old spots Highland cattle and wildlife along marked trails; 1-year-old has open meadow to practise walking under supervision away from paths.
places.baby_notes: Open meadow off marked paths safe ground for early walking practice, under supervision given roaming Highland cattle.
places.tips: No toilets on fælled itself — nearest at Islands Brygge, Byskoven or Ved Slusen.

places.name: Skydebanehaven
places.description: Behind the historic Neo-Gothic shooting-range wall, your 6-year-old can join staffed games, ride borrowed bikes and splash in the paddling pool, while the grassy lawn and sandbox give your 1-year-old safe space to crawl away from the bigger kids' equipment.
places.baby_notes: Grass lawn and sandbox area away from the climbing structures suit a crawling baby with supervision.
places.tips: Staff run activities most afternoons, so turn up after lunch for the best chance of borrowed toys.

places.name: Legepladsen på Sønder Boulevard – Trinidad
places.description: Your 6-year-old can clamber over the shipwrecked pirate boat, rope raft and slide, while the entire playground is covered in soft rubber safety surface so your 1-year-old can crawl and explore without injury risk.
places.baby_notes: The whole surface is soft rubber, so a crawling baby can move around the fenced site safely.
places.tips: Fully fenced, so it's one of the easier central playgrounds to let a toddler roam while watching an older child climb.

places.name: Den bemandede legeplads i Enghaveparken
places.description: Your 6-year-old can tackle the giant spider-web climbing net and zipline while staff run games, and your 1-year-old has a dedicated baby swing and sandbox area away from the bigger structures, plus a splash fountain on warm days.
places.baby_notes: A separate baby swing and sandbox corner sits apart from the big climbing net and zipline.
places.tips: The fountain playground only runs in the warmer months, so bring a spare set of clothes if visiting midday.

places.name: Den bemandede legeplads i Ørstedsparken
places.description: Copenhagen's second-oldest playground, from 1890, has an enclosed area built especially for younger children with a sandbox, low climbing frame and slide, letting your 1-year-old play separately while your 6-year-old joins the ball games and bigger climbing tower nearby.
places.baby_notes: The enclosed younger-children's section, separate from the ball-game area, gives a crawling baby a contained space.
places.tips: Pedagogical staff are on site most of the day and can point you to quieter corners if it's busy after school hours.

places.name: Den bemandede legeplads i Nørrebroparken (Bermudatrekanten)
places.description: Your 6-year-old can climb the giant whale, plane and ship structures across this 3,500 sqm staffed park, while open grass beside the equipment and an indoor activity house with board games give your 1-year-old calmer space away from the bigger kids.
places.baby_notes: Grass areas beside the play structures and the indoor activity house give a crawling baby room away from the bigger equipment.
places.tips: Ask staff about quieter hours — weekday mornings are calmest before school groups arrive.

places.name: Legepladsen Femte Juni Plads (Train Playground)
places.description: Your 6-year-old can ride the red train-themed structures, swings and carousel, while your 1-year-old has a separate cosy toddler playroom, for ages one to three, with board games, mini-swings and a sandbox just for the youngest visitors.
places.baby_notes: A dedicated 1-3 year old toddler playroom with sandbox and mini-swings sits apart from the main train structures.
places.tips: The toddler playroom is the quietest corner — a good retreat if the main train structures are swarmed by school-age kids.

places.name: Den bemandede legeplads i Lindevangsparken
places.description: Your 6-year-old can splash through the electronic water playground and join staffed activities, while the enclosed, shaded 3,200 sqm site gives your 1-year-old a safe, contained lawn to crawl on away from the road.
places.baby_notes: The fully enclosed, shaded site keeps a crawling baby contained and away from traffic.
places.tips: The splash basin only flows in summer, so pack swimwear for hot days.

places.name: Trafiklegepladsen i Fælledparken
places.description: Your 6-year-old can pedal borrowed bikes and karts around a child-sized traffic city with real signs and crossings, while a separate regular playground area with sandbox and swings gives your 1-year-old somewhere to play clear of the moving bikes.
places.baby_notes: The separate sandbox and swing area sits clear of the bike-traffic circuit, safe for a crawling baby.
places.tips: Keep a close eye near the bike paths — this is one playground where the older kids' zone genuinely has moving traffic.

places.name: Den bemandede legeplads i Lergravsparken
places.description: Your 6-year-old can conquer the giant yellow spider-web climbing net and zipline, while dedicated sandboxes for younger children give your 1-year-old a separate, safe spot to dig and crawl on Amager.
places.baby_notes: Sandboxes set aside for younger children are separate from the giant climbing net and zipline area.
places.tips: It's right by Lergravsparken metro station, making it an easy stop between Amager sights.

places.name: Konditaget Lüders
places.description: Your 6-year-old can run the rooftop running track and climb the play equipment 24 metres above Nordhavn, while the open grassy mounds well back from the edges give your 1-year-old a calm, fenced spot to crawl with a harbour view.
places.baby_notes: Grassy mounds set back from the rooftop edges give a crawling baby a fenced, calm patch away from the play equipment.
places.tips: It gets breezy up top, so bring an extra layer even in August.

places.name: KU.BE
places.description: Your 6-year-old can tackle the climbing labyrinth, slide and running track across KU.BE's four floors, while a dedicated baby and toddler play area on the ground floor gives your 1-year-old a soft, safe space to crawl, separate from the older kids' equipment.
places.baby_notes: The ground-floor baby and toddler area has a soft floor designed for crawling, separate from the upper-floor climbing equipment.
places.tips: Remove your shoes at the door — bring socks or indoor shoes for everyone, including the baby.

places.name: Legepladsen på Hauser Plads
places.description: This pocket-sized playground behind the old townhouses gives your 6-year-old low stone stumps and mounds to hop across, while its small scale and light footfall mean your 1-year-old can crawl on the grass without bigger kids charging past.
places.baby_notes: Small scale and low footfall let a crawling baby use the grass patch without bigger kids running through.
places.tips: Handy for a five-minute break between Strøget shopping and Kultorvet.

places.name: Legepladsen på Nikolaj Plads
places.description: Tucked behind Nikolaj Kirke just off Strøget, this artist-designed 'stylised forest' gives your 6-year-old low climbing branches to explore, while the compact, quiet square lets your 1-year-old crawl safely close to the bench where you're resting.
places.baby_notes: The small, quiet square keeps a crawling baby close by while an older sibling explores the low climbing structures.
places.tips: A good five-minute stop if you're shopping on Strøget and need to let little legs run.

places.name: Legepladsen på Sankt Annæ Plads
places.description: Your 6-year-old can run and climb over the grassy mounds and play sculpture, while the partly enclosed, shaded section near Amalienborg gives your 1-year-old a soft patch of grass to crawl on between sightseeing stops.
places.baby_notes: The partly enclosed, shaded grass mounds give a crawling baby a soft patch away from the open square.
places.tips: Perfect five-minute detour if you're walking between Nyhavn and Amalienborg.

places.name: Restaurant Tight
places.description: Large parts of the menu are marked GF so the 6-year-old can pick a gluten-free kids burger without special requests, and a high chair lets the 1-year-old sit close to the table through the relaxed lunch.
places.tips: Book ahead for weekend lunch — it fills with local families.

places.name: Gorm's i Magstræde
places.description: The 6-year-old can order a whole certified gluten-free pizza baked in colour-coded pans to avoid cross-contact, and the old half-timbered dining room has room for a highchair for the 1-year-old.
places.tips: Ask for the sealed gluten-free dough box — baked separately from the wheat pizzas.

places.name: H.U.G Bageri
places.description: Everything in the shop is 100% gluten-free, so the 6-year-old can pick any pastry from the counter unsupervised, and the 1-year-old can be fed a piece of bread here with no cross-contact worry.
places.tips: Go before midday — the celiac-safe pastries sell out.

places.name: Halifax Frederiksberg
places.description: The 6-year-old can build their own burger on a gluten-free bun that holds together well, while the casual format and high chairs keep the 1-year-old settled through the meal.
places.tips: Mention the gluten-free bun request when ordering at the counter.

places.name: RizRaz
places.description: The 6-year-old gets a proper kids menu of meatballs, pasta or pancakes, and the free supervised play room lets the 1-year-old crawl and toddle safely while the adults work through the vegetarian buffet.
places.baby_notes: The supervised children's play room gives the 1-year-old a safe floor to crawl on while adults eat.
places.tips: Buffet allergen labels aren't fully reliable — flag the gluten allergy to staff directly.

places.name: For Emma
places.description: This dedicated gluten-free, vegan and lactose-free bakery lets the 6-year-old choose any cake freely, and there's a small seating counter where the 1-year-old can be held while the family shares a treat.
places.tips: Frozen gluten-free pizza dough and bread are sold here too, useful for self-catering.

places.name: Glean
places.description: This 100% vegan, gluten-free stall inside the covered Torvehallerne market lets the 6-year-old try a plant-based flødebolle, and the wide indoor market aisles are easy to push the 1-year-old through in a pram.
places.tips: Torvehallerne has dozens of other stalls too, so a fussy toddler always has a backup.

places.name: BOB – Biomio Organic Bistro
places.description: A dedicated children's corner with toys lets the 1-year-old crawl and play safely while the 6-year-old eats from the organic bistro menu, which accommodates gluten-free diets on request.
places.baby_notes: The children's corner has toys and floor space for the 1-year-old to crawl near the table.
places.tips: Mention the gluten-free requirement when booking so the kitchen can prep in advance.

places.name: Vaffelbageren
places.description: The 6-year-old can pick a hand-made ice cream cone while the 1-year-old is held on a lap at the quayside tables, and an individually packaged gluten-free waffle is available on request.
places.tips: Keep the pram brake on at the quay tables — the quay slopes gently toward the water.

places.name: Emmerys
places.description: The organic bakery counter has gluten-free bread and cakes the 6-year-old can choose from, and the café seating gives enough room to park the pram next to the table for the 1-year-old.
places.tips: Gluten-free stock varies by location and time of day — ask before queueing.

places.name: Spuntino
places.description: The tapas-style sharing plates and pizzas suit the 6-year-old for picking at food family-style, and staff will prepare gluten-free pasta on request even though it isn't printed on the menu; the 1-year-old sits in a high chair at the table.
places.tips: Ask for gluten-free pasta explicitly — it exists but isn't listed on the printed menu.

places.name: Andersen Bakery
places.description: This Japanese-Danish bakery lets the 6-year-old pick from some gluten-free items at the counter, and it's a short pram walk from the Islands Brygge waterfront if the 1-year-old needs a walk afterward.
places.tips: Gluten-free selection is small — confirm what's in stock before committing.

places.name: Hooked Nørrebro
places.description: Casual fish-and-chips joint where the 6-year-old can order from the dedicated kids' menu of crispy fish bites and fries. The 1-year-old sits in a highchair at the table while the family shares fried seafood plates.
places.tips: Arrive before 12:30 to beat the lunch queue.

places.name: Sankt Peders Bageri
places.description: Copenhagen's oldest bakery, famous for its giant Wednesday cinnamon snail — the 6-year-old can pick a pastry from the counter while the 1-year-old naps in the pram parked by the door.
places.tips: Go on a Wednesday for the onsdagssnegl, but expect a queue.

places.name: Hart Bageri Frederiksberg
places.description: Sourdough bakery with a few window seats where the 6-year-old can pick a bun from the display and the 1-year-old can be held on a lap while adults have coffee.
places.tips: Morning visits have the best selection before items sell out.

places.name: Juno the Bakery
places.description: Small neighbourhood bakery famous for cardamom buns; the 6-year-old can watch pastries through the counter glass while the 1-year-old stays in the pram just inside the door.
places.tips: Popular buns sell out by early afternoon, go before noon.

places.name: Lagkagehuset (Ole & Steen), Christianshavn
places.description: Reliable Danish bakery chain with tables to sit down; the 6-year-old can pick a sandwich or pastry and the 1-year-old can have a gluten-free chocolate cake slice while parents grab coffee.
places.tips: Has proper seating, useful for a quick sit-down break with a pram.

places.name: Torvehallerne
places.description: Covered food market with dozens of stalls; the 6-year-old can choose their own lunch stall-by-stall while the 1-year-old has room to cruise along the wide aisles between stalls and communal tables.
places.baby_notes: Wide covered aisles and communal tables give a toddler room to cruise or crawl briefly away from stall counters.
places.tips: Go outside peak lunch hour (12-13:00) for open table seats.

places.name: Restaurant Karla
places.description: Classic Danish smørrebrød spot near Tivoli; the 6-year-old can try meatballs and fries from the child-friendly dishes while the 1-year-old sits in a highchair at the table.
places.tips: Convenient stop between Tivoli and the Glyptotek.

places.name: Sporvejen
places.description: Burger bar fitted out like an old tram; the 6-year-old can share a simple burger and fries while the 1-year-old is held or seated in a highchair at the compact tables.
places.tips: Small dining room fills fast at midday, arrive early.

places.name: Meyers Bageri, Jægersborggade
places.description: Neighbourhood bakery on a car-free, buggy-friendly street; the 6-year-old can pick a cinnamon roll while the 1-year-old rides in the pram along the pedestrian street outside.
places.tips: Combine with a stroll along car-free Jægersborggade.

places.name: Grød Christianshavn
places.description: Porridge-only café with simple, soft food that suits both ages; the 6-year-old can pick a sweet topping bowl while the 1-year-old eats plain porridge off a spoon in a highchair.
places.tips: Limited opening hours (check site) — not open every day.

places.name: Søndermarken
places.description: A sloping, car-free park where the 6-year-old can run the grassy hills and use the Bag Søndermarken playground, while the 1-year-old crawls safely on soft lawn away from paths. Free, open around the clock, and quiet enough for a calm walk before bedtime.
places.baby_notes: Wide grassy slopes away from paths let a walking 1-year-old crawl or toddle safely.
places.tips: Enter from Roskildevej side for the flattest pram route to the playground.

places.name: Kastrup Søbad
places.description: A striking circular wooden sea bath on Øresund where the 6-year-old can dip toes from the sunset-facing steps, while the 1-year-old stays safe in the pram on the boardwalk taking in the boats. Free and open year-round, with a calm, no-crowds feel in the early evening.
places.baby_notes: Open water and decking mean it's a hold-in-arms visit, not a floor-crawl spot for the baby.
places.tips: Go an hour before sunset for the calmest light and fewest people.

places.name: Tycho Brahe Planetarium
places.description: A domed IMAX-style theatre where the 6-year-old watches a short show about planets and stars, while the 1-year-old can nap in the pram in the foyer if the dome's darkness and sound feel too much. Evening slots run right up to bedtime on several weekdays.
places.baby_notes: Dome shows are dark and loud; the baby is better off napping in the pram in the foyer than inside the theatre.
places.tips: Check the day's programme for an English-narration slot before booking.

places.name: Pico Pizza Nørrebro
places.description: A casual sourdough-pizza spot where the 6-year-old picks three mini pizzas to share family-style, while the 1-year-old sits in a high chair nearby. Vegan and gluten-free pizzas are on the menu, and outdoor heated seating keeps things relaxed for an early dinner.
places.baby_notes: Restaurant floor isn't a crawl space, but the pram fits at the table and a high chair is available.
places.tips: Book ahead on weekends; the mini-pizza trio format suits sharing across ages.

places.name: Kalvebod Bølge
places.description: A wave-shaped timber harbour promenade where the 6-year-old can run up and down the rolling boardwalk levels, while the 1-year-old crawls on the grassy lawn at its base. Free, open-air, and an easy wind-down stroll after dinner.
places.baby_notes: Flat grassy lawn at the base of the wave is safe for crawling, away from the raised boardwalk levels.
places.tips: Keep small children off the steepest boardwalk sections; the lawn side is calmer.
